label: Current authorization wait
why: Set from the AMRPA survey average of just over 2.5 days for inpatient rehabilitation decisions. The survey did not measure skilled nursing facilities. The model applies the same wait to both, which is an assumption.

label: Faster authorization wait
why: An illustrative scenario, not a forecast. Rules allow up to 72 hours for expedited and seven calendar days for standard MA decisions. The AHIP pledge aims for real-time answers to most electronic approvals in 2027.

label: Variable cost of one extra waiting day
why: About a quarter of KFF's $3,297 expense per adjusted inpatient day (2024, from the AHA Annual Survey), on the reasoning that most staffing, overhead and capital costs do not change with one more low-acuity day. One academic center study found the last full day of a stay cost $420 in 1990s dollars, or 2.4 percent of total stay cost. MedPAC says some hospital costs are fixed and do not rise with a longer stay.

label: Share of freed bed-days refilled
why: An assumption: the share rises from 0% at 70% occupancy to 100% at 90%. National staffed-bed occupancy was 75.3% in the year after the public health emergency, and 85% is a shortage threshold in the Leuchter model. In a hospital benchmarking study, boarding exceeded 4 hours in 88.9% of hospital-months when occupancy passed 85%. Median occupancy in the FY{latestFy} cost reports is {medianOcc}, which suggests available beds exceed staffed beds. Override this if your hospital routinely turns patients away.

label: Where MA patients go after discharge
value: Home 65%, home health 17%, skilled nursing 15%, inpatient rehabilitation 2.5%
why: From MedPAC's 2023 data: 65, 17 and 15 percent for home, home health and skilled nursing. MedPAC combines inpatient rehabilitation and long-term care hospitals at 3 percent. The model uses 2.5 percent for rehabilitation and leaves out long-term care hospitals.

label: Which gap counts as excess
why: Unadjusted and adjusted gaps by discharge destination come from MedPAC Table 4-1. The placement lens is the adjusted gap minus the adjusted gap for patients discharged home, so it shows the extra stay length associated with post-acute placement. MedPAC describes these gaps as associations and says they suggest that plans could slow discharges through activities such as prior authorization.
